heldout_pairing.why: Same capability (resolving deferred annotations for parametrized generics), opposite direction: the public demand covers unstructuring, the held-out one covers structuring, and upstream fixed them in two separate call sites.
Same capability (an abstract collection annotation must produce the immutable variant), different collection: sequences in the public demand, sets in the held-out one.
Same capability (walking a class hierarchy for the tagged subclass strategy), different degenerate shape: a generic parent in the public demand, a multiply-reachable leaf in the held-out one.

Same capability (per-field settings carried on the field annotation), different modelled shapes: attrs classes and dataclasses in the public demand, TypedDicts and dict-shaped NamedTuples in the held-out one; upstream implemented them in separate hook-factory modules.

rejected_candidates.reason: tomlkit preconf date handling. The evaluator environment has no tomlkit installed, so no contract can exercise cattrs.preconf.tomlkit at all.

New cattrs.preconf.tomllib module. The demand would essentially be 'create a module and a factory under exactly this dotted name', so the contract would degrade into a naming check rather than a capability check; the writing side also needs tomli-w, which the evaluator environment does not have.

configure_tagged_union with recursive type aliases. A real behavioral fix, but the window already yields two contracts in the include_subclasses / configure_tagged_union family (pr_683 public, pr_713 held-out); adding a third would concentrate the Pack on one subsystem. Kept as a surplus candidate beyond the 16-contract target.

Aliases generate rename metadata in generated hooks. End-to-end un/structuring already produces the right keys on the starter; the only difference is the introspection metadata hanging off the generated hook, so a contract would bind to an internal metadata shape rather than to observable conversion behavior.
Enum hook factories. Behaviorally equivalent to pr_702, which is already covered; the only genuinely new surface is the cattrs.enums module name, which would make the contract a naming check.
The opt-out half of pr_668. The default-on half is already a public demand; a separate contract could only assert that this specific keyword argument exists, which is a naming check.
